domains.name: Player fairness
domains.promise: Any member can queue tracks with /play; a requester can always instantly skip their own currently playing track; skipping anyone else's track requires a listener-majority vote among the humans in the voice channel; an optional dashboard-configured DJ role adds arbitration powers (force-skip, stop, volume, filters, remove); a requester can reposition their own queued tracks; and queue priority can be raised by member votes. All fairness rules are enforced per guild with owner-branded messaging.

controls.description: Discord role id granting DJ arbitration powers (force-skip, /stop, /volume, /loop, /shuffle, /seek, /remove, /pause, /filter). Empty string means no DJ role is configured and arbitration falls back to the guild owner only. Set via the dashboard Music page (guild_config.dj_role_id).
Percentage of non-bot listeners in the voice channel whose votes are required for a vote-skip of another member's track to pass. Votes needed = ceil(listeners * threshold / 100).
When true, the requester of the currently playing track can skip it instantly with /skip, without a vote and without the DJ role.
When true, a member can reposition their own queued (not yet played) tracks within the queue; moving or removing another member's track still requires the DJ role.

When true, members can cast priority votes on upcoming queue entries; entries with more priority votes are promoted ahead of same-requester entries with fewer votes, never displacing the currently playing track.

defaults.rationale: Owner decision: the DJ role is optional arbitration, not a prerequisite. Out of the box no DJ role exists and fairness is governed by self-skip plus listener-majority voting.
Owner decision: listener-majority vote-skip. 50 percent with ceiling rounding reproduces ceil(listeners / 2), a simple majority of humans in the voice channel.
Owner decision: you can always skip your own track. This is the member-respectful default and stays on unless the owner deliberately disables it.
Owner decision: requesters manage their own queued tracks. Members keep agency over their own picks without needing DJ powers.
Owner decision: voting-based priority is part of the fairness model and is on by default so popular picks rise without DJ intervention.

permissions.actor: Any guild member connected to a voice channel
permissions.action: Add a track or playlist to the shared queue with /play
permissions.enforcement: The /play handler only requires voice-channel presence and a text channel; no role gate is applied before queueing.

permissions.actor: The member who requested the currently playing track
permissions.action: Instantly skip their own currently playing track with /skip
permissions.enforcement: The /skip handler compares the invoking user id to the current entry's requestedBy and bypasses both the vote and the DJ check on match while self-skip-enabled is true.

permissions.actor: A member without the DJ role who did not request the current track
permissions.action: Force-skip another member's currently playing track without a vote
permissions.enforcement: The /skip handler routes non-requester non-DJ invocations into the vote-skip tally; no immediate skip occurs until the listener-majority threshold is met.

permissions.actor: A member holding the configured DJ role, or the guild owner
permissions.enforcement: isDJ resolves true for the guild owner and holders of guild_config.dj_role_id; arbitration handlers check isDJ before acting.

permissions.actor: The member who requested a queued, not-yet-played track
permissions.action: Reposition their own entry within the upcoming queue
permissions.enforcement: The queue move surface verifies the target entry's requestedBy matches the invoker before calling the queue manager's moveEntry, while requester-move-enabled is true.

permissions.actor: A member without the DJ role
permissions.action: Move or remove another member's queued track
permissions.enforcement: Move and /remove requests against entries requested by someone else are rejected with the fairness-denied message unless the invoker passes the isDJ check.

messages.trigger: A member successfully adds a track with /play
messages.surface: Discord embed reply in the invoking text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: {track-title} is queued at spot {queue-position} — nice pick, {requester}!

messages.trigger: The requester skips their own currently playing track
messages.surface: Discord embed reply in the invoking text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: {requester} skipped their own pick {track-title} — on to the next one!

messages.trigger: A non-requester casts a vote-skip that does not yet reach the threshold
messages.surface: Discord embed reply in the invoking text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: Vote to move past {track-title}: {votes} of {votes-needed} listeners agree.

messages.trigger: The vote-skip tally reaches the listener-majority threshold
messages.surface: Discord embed reply in the invoking text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: The listeners have spoken — {track-title} steps aside for {next-title}.

messages.trigger: A member attempts a direct action on another member's track without DJ powers
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed reply to the invoker
messages.defaultTemplate: Only {requester} or a DJ can control {track-title} directly — cast a vote instead.

messages.trigger: The vote store cannot record a skip or priority vote
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed reply to the invoker
messages.defaultTemplate: Your vote on {track-title} did not go through — please try again in a moment.

messages.trigger: The audio backend fails while a track is playing
messages.surface: Discord embed in the queue's bound text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: The player hit a snag on {track-title}: {reason}. Hold tight while we recover.

messages.trigger: Priority votes promote a queued entry to an earlier spot
messages.surface: Discord embed in the queue's bound text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: {track-title} moved up to spot {queue-position} with {vote-count} priority votes.

values.description: No active playback session in the guild; the bot is not in voice and no fairness rules are engaged.
A track is playing; the requester, DJ arbitration, and vote thresholds for the current track are known and enforced.
At least one vote-skip has been cast against the current track and the tally is below the listener-majority threshold.
The audio backend is unavailable; playback is halted but the queue, requester attribution, and vote state remain persisted for recovery.

transitions.trigger: A member in a voice channel runs /play with a resolvable query
transitions.expectedEffect: The bot joins the voice channel, the queue is created, the track plays, and the entry records the requester's user id.

transitions.trigger: A listener who is not the requester and not a DJ runs /skip
transitions.expectedEffect: One vote is recorded for that user, the vote-progress message shows votes versus votes-needed computed from current non-bot listeners.

transitions.trigger: The recorded votes from current listeners reach ceil(listeners * threshold / 100)
transitions.expectedEffect: The current track is skipped exactly once, the vote tally is cleared, and the next track starts with its own fresh vote state.

transitions.trigger: The current track ends naturally, is self-skipped by its requester, or is force-skipped by a DJ
transitions.expectedEffect: The pending vote tally is discarded so no votes carry over to the next track.

transitions.trigger: The requester of the current track runs /skip while self-skip-enabled is true
transitions.expectedEffect: The track is skipped immediately without any vote, the self-skip-confirm message posts, and playback advances to the next entry.

transitions.trigger: The Lavalink audio node disconnects or errors mid-track
transitions.expectedEffect: Playback halts, the playback-error message posts, the persisted queue and vote state are untouched, and automatic reconnection begins.
Playback resumes with the persisted current entry and requester attribution intact; no duplicate track entries are created.

transitions.trigger: The queue ends, a DJ runs /stop, or the auto-leave timer for an empty voice channel elapses
transitions.expectedEffect: The bot leaves voice, the vote tally is cleared, and the session closes with an audit record.

failures.trigger: The Lavalink node is unreachable while a track is playing or a /play resolution is requested
failures.expectedBehavior: Playback halts without corrupting the persisted queue; the channel receives the playback-error message; reconnection retries automatically; no track entries or votes are lost or duplicated.

failures.trigger: The Valkey vote set cannot be read or written when a member casts a vote
failures.expectedBehavior: The vote is treated as not recorded, the invoker receives the vote-error message, and no skip fires from an indeterminate tally; the tally is re-evaluated on the next successful vote.

failures.trigger: A member without DJ powers attempts to force-skip, remove, or move another member's track
failures.expectedBehavior: The action is denied with the ephemeral fairness-denied message pointing to the vote path; playback and queue state are unchanged; the denial is audited.

evidence.observer: Harness Discord client joined to the run-prefixed test guild's voice and text channels
evidence.expectedObservation: Fairness embeds (track-queued, self-skip-confirm, vote-progress, vote-skip-complete, fairness-denied) appear in the bound text channel with correct requester attribution and the bot audibly starts, skips, and stops tracks in voice.

evidence.observer: Supabase client using an anon key scoped to a non-member user versus the service role
evidence.expectedObservation: guild_config rows carrying dj_role_id and fairness settings are readable and writable only through owner-scoped paths; the anon probe against another guild's row returns zero rows.

evidence.observer: Audit log reader querying music.* events for the run-prefixed guild
evidence.expectedObservation: Skip, vote-skip pass, fairness denial, and backend failure events each produce exactly one immutable audit row; no audit rows are deleted during or after the run.

evidence.observer: Harness inbox for the owner notification channel (owner DM or configured notification route)
evidence.expectedObservation: The owner is notified exactly once per audio-backend outage episode with guild, track, and reason context; routine skips and denials produce no owner noise.

evidence.observer: Embed inspector over every fairness message captured in the run
evidence.expectedObservation: All player-fairness embeds use the guild's configured brand name, colors, and tone preset, and carry the subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution in the footer.

evidence.observer: Interaction replayer re-delivering recorded /skip and vote interactions plus queue-state differ
evidence.expectedObservation: Replaying a delivered /skip or vote interaction advances the queue zero additional times and records zero additional votes; one user never counts twice in a tally.

evidence.observer: Post-run sweeper listing run-prefixed Valkey keys, guild_config rows, and Discord channels/messages
evidence.expectedObservation: All run-prefixed queues, vote sets, config rows, and test messages created by fairness scenarios are removed; audit rows remain by design.

scenarios.promise: Out of the box, with no DJ role configured, any member can queue; a requester self-skips instantly; a non-requester's /skip opens a listener-majority vote instead of force-skipping.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Member A queues two tracks and self-skips the first instantly; member B's /skip on A's second track records one vote and posts vote-progress showing 1 of 2 with two humans listening; the track keeps playing until the majority is reached.

assertions.expectedObservation: track-queued, self-skip-confirm, and vote-progress embeds appear in order; B's lone /skip does not stop the audible track.
The run guild's guild_config row shows dj_role_id null and is unreadable via the anon probe from a non-member context.
One music.self_skip audit row for A and one music.vote_cast row for B exist; no music.force_skip row exists for B.
No owner notification is sent for routine default-path playback and voting.
All embeds in the flow use the default playful tone preset with the guild brand name and powered-by-SomniBot footer.
Re-delivering B's vote interaction leaves the tally at exactly one vote.
Run-prefixed queue, vote keys, and test messages from this scenario are removed by the sweeper.

scenarios.promise: Configuring a DJ role on the dashboard grants arbitration: the DJ force-skips another member's track instantly, no vote required.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The owner sets dj_role_id to the run's DJ role via PUT /api/music; a DJ-role holder runs /skip on member A's playing track and it skips immediately with the vote tally untouched, while /stop, /volume, and /remove also succeed for the DJ.

assertions.expectedObservation: The DJ's /skip yields an immediate skip embed naming the next track; no vote-progress embed appears.
guild_config.dj_role_id equals the run DJ role id after the owner-scoped PUT; the write path rejected any non-owner session.
A music.force_skip audit row records the DJ actor, the skipped track, and the arbitration basis dj-role.
No owner notification fires for authorized DJ arbitration.
DJ arbitration embeds keep the guild brand voice and attribution footer identical to member-facing embeds.
Replaying the DJ's /skip interaction advances the queue no further than the single original skip.
The run DJ role assignment and config change are reverted and run-prefixed artifacts removed.

scenarios.promise: Raising vote-skip-threshold-percent to 100 makes vote-skip unanimous, proving the threshold control takes effect distinctly from SET-A.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With threshold 100 and three human listeners, two votes leave member A's track playing with vote-progress showing 2 of 3; the third listener's vote passes the tally and the track skips exactly once.

assertions.expectedObservation: vote-progress embeds show 1 of 3 then 2 of 3; vote-skip-complete posts only after the third distinct listener votes.
The threshold setting persisted for this guild only via the owner-scoped write path and reads back as 100.
Three music.vote_cast rows and exactly one music.vote_skip_passed row exist for the track.
No owner notification fires for a completed vote-skip.
The vote-skip-complete embed uses the configured brand tone and attribution footer.
Re-delivering the third voter's interaction does not skip a second track or restart the tally.
Vote sets and the threshold override are removed after the run.

scenarios.promise: Invalid fairness configuration is rejected atomically: a malformed DJ role id or an out-of-range vote threshold persists nothing.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: PUT /api/music with dj_role_id not-a-snowflake and a vote threshold of 0 returns a validation error; the stored config re-reads unchanged and live fairness behavior in Discord is unaffected.

assertions.expectedObservation: Fairness behavior in the guild (self-skip and majority voting) is identical before and after the rejected write.
guild_config re-reads byte-identical for the fairness columns; no partial field of the invalid payload was persisted.
A config.rejected audit row records the invalid payload attempt without storing the invalid values as applied state.
The dashboard session sees the inline validation error; no out-of-band owner alert is needed for the owner's own rejected input.
The dashboard validation error renders in the owner-branded dashboard shell.
Replaying the invalid PUT produces the same rejection and still persists nothing.
No residual invalid values exist anywhere; run-prefixed session artifacts are removed.

scenarios.promise: Non-DJ members cannot exercise arbitration and non-owners cannot change fairness settings.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: A non-DJ member's /stop, /remove on another member's track, and /volume are each denied ephemerally with fairness guidance; a logged-in non-owner's PUT /api/music returns a permission error and changes nothing.

assertions.expectedObservation: Each denied command yields an ephemeral fairness-denied or DJ-required embed; playback continues uninterrupted.
The non-owner PUT is blocked by requireGuildOwner and direct table access under the non-owner's JWT is denied by RLS.
music.fairness_denied audit rows record each denied attempt with actor and attempted action.
No owner notification is sent for routine permission denials.
Denial embeds keep the playful-but-clear brand tone and attribution footer rather than raw error text.
Replaying a denied interaction produces the same denial and no state change.
No artifacts beyond audit rows persist from denied attempts; run-prefixed test users and messages are removed.

scenarios.promise: When the audio backend dies mid-track, fairness state fails safe: playback halts, the queue and votes are preserved, and members get a branded explanation.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Stopping the Lavalink container mid-track posts the playback-error message, the session enters degraded, the persisted queue including requester attribution and the open vote tally are intact, and no track is skipped or duplicated.

assertions.expectedObservation: The playback-error embed posts once in the bound text channel with the track title and reason.
Persisted queue and config rows for the guild are unchanged by the outage and remain guild-scoped.
Exactly one music.playback_backend_failed audit row exists for the outage episode.
The owner receives one notification identifying the guild and the backend outage.
The failure message uses the owner-branded reassuring voice, not a stack trace.
The outage grants no skips: the vote tally and current index re-read identical before and after the failure.
After the run the restored backend and run-prefixed state are torn down cleanly.

scenarios.promise: After a transient audio-backend outage, automatic retry converges: playback resumes the same current entry with fairness state intact.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Restarting the Lavalink container leads the bot to reconnect automatically and resume the persisted current track; the requester can still self-skip and the pre-outage vote tally still counts toward the same track's threshold.

assertions.expectedObservation: Audible playback resumes for the same track without a duplicate track-queued embed; a subsequent self-skip works normally.
The queue record shows the same entries and currentIndex after recovery as before the outage.
One recovery audit row follows the failure row; retries do not multiply audit entries per attempt loop.
At most one recovery notice follows the outage notification; retry attempts do not spam the owner.
Any recovery message uses the brand voice and attribution footer.
Reconnect attempts never double-start the track: exactly one live player exists for the guild after convergence.
Retry timers and run-prefixed state are fully cleared after the run.

scenarios.promise: Duplicate delivery of skip and vote interactions never yields duplicate skips or double-counted votes.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Re-delivering a recorded self-skip interaction advances the queue zero additional positions, and re-delivering a vote interaction leaves the voter's contribution at exactly one; the same user invoking /skip twice on the same track is told they already voted.

assertions.expectedObservation: The second identical vote attempt yields an already-voted ephemeral reply and no tally increase in any subsequent vote-progress embed.
The vote set for the track contains the user id exactly once and the queue currentIndex advanced exactly once for the self-skip.
One audit row exists per unique logical action; replayed deliveries add no rows.
Replays generate zero owner notifications.
The already-voted reply keeps the brand tone and attribution footer.
End-state queue and vote structures are byte-identical between single delivery and duplicate delivery runs.
Replay fixtures and run-prefixed state are removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: Fairness state survives a full stack restart: requester attribution and the open vote tally persist so no one gains or loses skip rights.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With a vote at 1 of 2 on member A's track, the bot process is killed and restarted; after recovery A can still self-skip, the surviving tally still counts, and one additional listener vote completes the majority for the same track.

assertions.expectedObservation: After restart, one more vote triggers vote-skip-complete for the same track; A's self-skip rights are honored identically pre- and post-restart.
The persisted queue in Valkey and config in Supabase re-read unchanged across the restart with requestedBy intact.
Audit rows from before the restart remain and post-restart rows continue the same episode without duplication.
A planned harness restart produces no spurious outage notification once recovery completes within the grace window.
Post-restart messages carry identical branding config with no default-brand flash.
Restart-time recovery does not re-fire completed skips: the queue advances only from post-restart actions.
Restart artifacts and run-prefixed keys are removed after the run.

scenarios.promise: Concurrent final votes and a simultaneous self-skip resolve to exactly one queue advance.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Two listeners cast the threshold-completing votes concurrently while the requester issues a self-skip in the same window; the queue advances exactly one position, exactly one skip message posts, and the vote tally is cleared once.

assertions.expectedObservation: Exactly one skip-completion embed posts for the contested track; later actors receive follow-up state rather than a second skip.
The queue currentIndex advanced by exactly one and the vote set for the old track is deleted exactly once.
One skip audit row exists for the track regardless of how many concurrent actors raced.
The race produces no owner notification.
All replies in the race window remain branded and coherent with the single-skip outcome.
The concurrent losers' interactions are absorbed idempotently with no double advance.
Race fixtures and run-prefixed state are removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: Fairness state is strictly guild-scoped: votes, DJ roles, and thresholds in one guild never affect another.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With sessions running in guilds A and B, votes cast in A never appear in B's tally, A's DJ role grants nothing in B, and changing A's threshold leaves B's voting math unchanged.

assertions.expectedObservation: Guild B's vote-progress numbers are unaffected by activity in guild A, and A's DJ is denied arbitration in B.
Vote keys and config rows are keyed per guild; the anon probe from B's context cannot read A's config row.
Audit rows carry the correct guild id and no cross-guild rows appear.
Notifications route to each guild's own owner only.
Each guild's embeds use that guild's own brand config simultaneously.
Replaying guild A interactions changes nothing in guild B.
Both guilds' run-prefixed artifacts are independently and completely removed.

scenarios.promise: Every fairness scenario's run-prefixed resources are enumerable and fully removed, leaving only immutable audit rows.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: After the fairness suite, a sweep finds zero run-prefixed Valkey queue or vote keys, zero run-prefixed config overrides, zero leftover test messages or roles, and the audit trail intact.

assertions.expectedObservation: Run-created channels, roles, and messages are deleted from the test guilds.
Run-prefixed config rows are removed or reverted; remaining rows contain no run identifiers.
Audit rows from the run remain present and unmodified, honoring never-delete.
Cleanup completes without sending owner notifications.
Brand configuration is restored to its pre-run values.
Running the sweeper twice is idempotent and reports zero remaining resources both times.
The final inventory of run-prefixed resources across Discord, Valkey, and Supabase is empty.

domains.name: Collaborative queue
domains.promise: The guild's shared music queue is a persistent, collaborative object: every mutation is durably stored so the queue and playback position survive bot and stack restarts; capacity guardrails keep it fair; and the owner configures enablement, default volume, DJ role, idle timeouts, and capacity from the dashboard Music page with changes applied live.

controls.description: Master switch for the music feature in the guild (guild_config.music_enabled). When false, music commands decline politely with an owner-branded notice.
Volume applied when a new queue session starts (guild_config.music_default_volume), matching the /volume command range.
Minutes the bot waits alone in an empty voice channel before leaving (guild_config.music_auto_leave_minutes).
Minutes of paused or inactive playback before the session is destroyed and the queue cleared (guild_config.music_auto_destroy_minutes).
Maximum total entries allowed in the guild queue; additions beyond the cap are declined with the queue-full message rather than silently trimmed.
Maximum queued entries a single member may hold at once (not counting the playing track), preventing queue monopolization.
Whether the same track URI may appear in the queue more than once. When false, duplicate additions are declined with a friendly notice.

defaults.rationale: Owner theme: every feature works perfectly out of the box; music is live the moment the bot joins.
Matches the shipped dashboard and bot default of 50, a comfortable mid-level that respects listeners on first use.
Matches the shipped default: five minutes alone in voice before leaving balances persistence with not squatting in channels.
Matches the shipped default: thirty minutes of inactivity before the session and queue are cleaned up.
Matches the enforced storage guardrail of five thousand entries, well within the serialized-state budget.
Matches the enforced per-user guardrail of fifty entries so no single member monopolizes the collaborative queue.
Member-respectful default: repeat requests are a normal part of shared listening; owners who dislike repeats can turn it off.

permissions.actor: Any guild member connected to a voice channel
permissions.action: Append tracks or playlists to the shared queue with /play, subject to capacity guardrails
permissions.enforcement: The /play handler requires only voice presence; the queue manager enforces max-queue-length and per-user-queue-cap on insert.

permissions.action: View the queue and now-playing state with /queue and /np
permissions.enforcement: Read-only queue commands have no role gate and render pages from the persisted queue.

permissions.actor: A member without the DJ role
permissions.action: Stop the session or clear the entire shared queue
permissions.enforcement: The /stop handler requires isDJ; non-DJ attempts receive an ephemeral DJ-required denial and the queue is untouched.

permissions.actor: The guild owner authenticated on the dashboard
permissions.action: Read and update music settings via the dashboard Music page and PUT /api/music
permissions.enforcement: requireGuildOwner gates the API route; saved changes upsert guild_config and notify the bot to hot-reload.

permissions.actor: Any authenticated dashboard user who does not own the guild
permissions.action: Update music settings for the guild
permissions.enforcement: requireGuildOwner rejects the session before any write; Supabase RLS denies direct guild_config writes under the non-owner JWT.

messages.trigger: A track is durably appended to the shared queue
messages.surface: Discord embed reply in the invoking text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: {track-title} joins the queue at spot {queue-position} — {queue-length} tracks lined up!

messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed reply to the requester
messages.defaultTemplate: The queue is at its {max-entries}-track limit — let a few play out first.

messages.trigger: An addition would exceed the requester's per-user-queue-cap
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed reply to the requester
messages.defaultTemplate: {requester}, you already have {user-cap} tracks queued — share the aux for a bit!

messages.trigger: The bot recovers a persisted queue after a restart
messages.surface: Discord embed in the queue's bound text channel
messages.audience: All members of the text channel
messages.defaultTemplate: Back online — {queue-length} tracks restored, resuming with {track-title}.

messages.trigger: The owner saves music settings on the dashboard
messages.surface: Dashboard toast on the Music settings page
messages.defaultTemplate: Music settings for {guild-name} saved — changes are live in the server.

messages.trigger: The queue store is unreachable during a queue mutation
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed reply to the requester
messages.defaultTemplate: The queue store is unreachable — {track-title} was not added. Please try again shortly.

messages.trigger: Music settings cannot be loaded from the database at startup or reload
messages.defaultTemplate: Music settings for {guild-name} could not be loaded — running on safe defaults until they are back.

messages.trigger: A member uses a music command while music-enabled is false
messages.surface: Ephemeral Discord embed reply to the invoker
messages.defaultTemplate: Music is currently switched off in {guild-name} — an admin can flip it back on from the dashboard.

values.description: No queue object exists for the guild in the store; the bot is not in voice for music.
A persisted queue exists with entries, current index, loop mode, volume, and pause flag; every mutation is saved to the store before being acknowledged.
The queue exists but the voice channel is empty or playback is paused; the configured auto-leave or auto-destroy timer is running.
The bot process is down or the queue store is unreachable; the last durably saved queue state is authoritative for recovery.

transitions.trigger: The first successful /play in the guild
transitions.expectedEffect: A queue object is created and persisted with the session's voice and text channels, the configured default volume, and the first entries.

transitions.trigger: Any queue mutation: add, remove, move, shuffle, loop change, volume change, pause toggle, or track advance
transitions.expectedEffect: The full queue state is atomically saved to the store so a crash at any point loses at most the in-flight mutation, never the queue.

transitions.trigger: All human listeners leave the voice channel, or playback is paused with no resume
transitions.expectedEffect: The auto-leave (empty channel) or auto-destroy (inactivity) timer starts using the configured minutes.

transitions.trigger: A human listener rejoins or playback resumes before the timer elapses
transitions.expectedEffect: The pending timer is cancelled and the session continues with the same persisted queue.

transitions.trigger: The auto-leave or auto-destroy timer elapses
transitions.expectedEffect: The bot leaves voice, the queue and vote keys are deleted from the store, and the teardown is audited.

transitions.trigger: The bot process stops or the queue store becomes unreachable
transitions.expectedEffect: No destructive action occurs; the last saved queue state remains in the store as the recovery source.

transitions.trigger: The bot restarts and finds a persisted queue for the guild
transitions.expectedEffect: The queue, current index, volume, loop mode, and pause flag are reloaded; playback resumes and the queue-restored message posts; if the voice channel is empty the auto-leave timer starts immediately.

failures.trigger: Valkey is unreachable when a member attempts a queue mutation
failures.expectedBehavior: The mutation is declined atomically with the queue-store-error message; no partial queue state is written; the current track keeps playing from the live player; the bot retries store connectivity automatically.

failures.trigger: guild_config cannot be read at startup or on a dashboard-triggered reload
failures.expectedBehavior: The session runs on the documented safe defaults (enabled, volume 50, 5 and 30 minute timers, caps 5000 and 50), the owner is notified via config-fallback, and the load retries automatically until the stored settings apply.

failures.trigger: An addition would exceed max-queue-length or the requester's per-user cap
failures.expectedBehavior: The addition is declined with the queue-full or user-cap-reached message; nothing is silently trimmed; existing entries and playback are untouched.

evidence.observer: Harness Discord client in the run-prefixed test guild's voice and text channels
evidence.expectedObservation: track-added, /queue pagination, queue-restored, and capacity-decline embeds render with correct positions, lengths, and requester attribution, and audible playback matches the persisted queue order.

evidence.observer: Supabase clients under owner, non-owner, and anon contexts plus a direct Valkey key inspector
evidence.expectedObservation: guild_config music columns are writable only through the owner-scoped route, unreadable cross-guild under anon, and queue state lives under guild-scoped keys only.

evidence.observer: Audit log reader querying music.* configuration and lifecycle events
evidence.expectedObservation: Config saves, session teardown, store outages, and capacity hits each produce exactly one immutable audit row; no audit rows are deleted.

evidence.observer: Harness inbox for the owner notification channel
evidence.expectedObservation: The owner is notified once per store outage or config-load failure episode with guild context; routine queue activity produces no owner noise.

evidence.observer: Embed and dashboard-shell inspector over all queue surfaces captured in the run
evidence.expectedObservation: Queue embeds and the dashboard Music page use the guild's brand name, colors, and tone with the subtle powered-by-SomniBot attribution.

evidence.observer: Interaction replayer plus queue-state differ across duplicate deliveries and crash-resume cycles
evidence.expectedObservation: Duplicate /play deliveries and crash-replayed mutations yield exactly one persisted entry per logical request and one confirmation embed.

evidence.observer: Post-run sweeper listing run-prefixed Valkey keys, guild_config rows, and Discord artifacts
evidence.expectedObservation: All run-prefixed queues, now-playing keys, config overrides, and test messages are removed; audit rows remain by design.

scenarios.promise: Out of the box, /play creates a persistent shared queue at volume 50, /queue shows every member's entries with attribution, and the queue object is durably stored per guild.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Two members each queue tracks; /queue lists all entries in order with each requester named; the store holds one guild-scoped queue object whose entries, currentIndex, and volume 50 match what Discord displays.

assertions.expectedObservation: track-added embeds show correct positions and the /queue embed lists both members' tracks with requester attribution at default volume 50.
Exactly one queue object exists under the run guild's key and no music config row was needed for defaults to work.
Session-start and track-add events are audited once each with the correct guild id.
Routine queue creation sends no owner notification.
Queue embeds use the default playful tone with guild brand name and powered-by-SomniBot footer.
Re-delivering one member's /play interaction leaves the queue length unchanged.
The run-prefixed queue and messages are removed by the sweeper.

scenarios.promise: Dashboard configuration takes effect live: lowering default volume and shortening auto-leave changes real session behavior without a bot restart.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The owner saves default-volume 25 and auto-leave-minutes 1 on the dashboard Music page; the settings-saved toast appears, the bot hot-reloads config, a new session starts at volume 25, and after all humans leave the voice channel the bot departs in about one minute.

assertions.expectedObservation: The new session's now-playing state reports volume 25 and the bot leaves the emptied voice channel within the one-minute window plus grace.
guild_config reads back music_default_volume 25 and music_auto_leave_minutes 1, written only via the owner-scoped PUT.
One config-save audit row records the owner, the changed fields, and prior values.
The owner sees the dashboard settings-saved toast; no additional out-of-band notification fires.
The dashboard Music page and toast render in the owner-branded shell.
Replaying the PUT is idempotent: the same values persist once with no duplicate audit spam per replayed request body.
Config values are restored to pre-run defaults and run artifacts removed.

scenarios.promise: A second distinct configuration proves independent effect: disabling music turns the feature off politely, and re-enabling restores it without data loss.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: The owner sets music-enabled false; /play and /queue decline with the music-disabled notice while the persisted queue object is retained; re-enabling makes the same queue usable again with its entries intact.

assertions.expectedObservation: While disabled, music commands reply ephemerally with the branded music-disabled notice; after re-enable, /queue shows the identical pre-disable entries.
guild_config.music_enabled toggles false then true via the owner route; the stored queue object is never deleted by the toggle.
Both toggle saves are audited with actor and prior value; no queue-destruction event appears.
Feature toggling by the owner produces no failure notifications.
The music-disabled notice names the guild brand, not SomniBot, as the voice of the server.
Replaying the disable PUT does not double-toggle or destroy the queue.
music_enabled is restored and run-prefixed artifacts removed.

scenarios.promise: Out-of-range music settings are rejected with a clear validation error and nothing is persisted — no silent clamping.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: PUT /api/music with default-volume 300, auto-leave-minutes 0, and auto-destroy-minutes 999 returns a validation error naming the offending fields; guild_config re-reads unchanged and live sessions keep their prior settings.

assertions.expectedObservation: A session started after the rejected write still uses the previously stored volume and timers.
The music columns of guild_config are byte-identical before and after the rejected request; no clamped values were written.
A config.rejected audit row records the invalid attempt without recording the invalid values as applied.
The owner sees the inline dashboard validation error; no out-of-band alert fires for their own rejected input.
The validation error message is rendered in the branded dashboard shell with actionable field-level text.
Replaying the invalid PUT is rejected identically and persists nothing.
No residue of the invalid payload exists in any store after the run.

scenarios.promise: Only the guild owner configures the queue: non-owner dashboard sessions and direct database writes are denied, and non-DJ members cannot clear the shared queue.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: A non-owner's GET and PUT against /api/music return a permission error; a direct guild_config write under the non-owner JWT is denied by RLS; a non-DJ member's /stop is refused ephemerally and the queue survives.

assertions.expectedObservation: The non-DJ /stop attempt yields an ephemeral DJ-required denial while playback and the queue continue.
requireGuildOwner blocks the API call and the RLS policy denies the direct table write; guild_config is unchanged.
Denied configuration and denied /stop attempts are each audited with actor identity.
Isolated denials produce no owner alert.
Denial responses use branded, respectful copy rather than raw authorization errors.
Replaying denied requests yields identical denials and zero state change.
Non-owner test sessions and run artifacts are removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: When the queue store goes down, mutations fail safe: members get a clear branded error, nothing is partially written, and the last saved state remains authoritative.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With Valkey stopped, a member's /play returns the queue-store-error message and no entry is recorded anywhere; the currently playing track finishes from the live player; the owner is notified once; when Valkey returns the queue re-reads exactly as last saved.

assertions.expectedObservation: The requester receives the queue-store-error embed and no phantom track-added embed ever appears.
After the store returns, the queue object is byte-identical to the last pre-outage save with no partial entry.
Exactly one music.queue_store_unavailable audit row exists for the outage episode.
The owner receives one outage notification naming the guild and the store dependency.
The failure copy is calm, branded, and instructs retry rather than exposing infrastructure detail.
The failed mutation grants nothing: retrying after recovery adds the track exactly once.
Outage fixtures are torn down and run-prefixed keys removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: Transient store failures converge under automatic retry: once connectivity returns, the same logical mutation lands exactly once.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: During a brief Valkey blip, the member retries /play after the branded error; post-recovery the queue contains exactly one copy of the track, config hot-reload retries also converge, and no duplicate confirmation embeds exist.

assertions.expectedObservation: Exactly one track-added embed for the track exists across the blip-and-retry sequence.
The persisted queue contains the track exactly once with a single requestedBy attribution.
The audit trail shows failure then success for the same logical request without per-attempt row multiplication.
At most one outage-and-recovery notification pair reaches the owner for the blip.
Retry-facing copy stays branded and consistent across attempts.
Automatic retries internal to the bot never insert the entry twice.
Blip fixtures and run-prefixed state are removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: Duplicate delivery of queue mutations never duplicates entries, confirmations, or config writes.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Re-delivering a recorded /play interaction, a /remove interaction, and a dashboard PUT each produce zero additional queue entries, zero additional removals, and zero additional config changes beyond the originals.

assertions.expectedObservation: No second track-added or removal embed appears for any replayed interaction.
Queue length, entry order, and guild_config values are identical between single-delivery and duplicate-delivery runs.
One audit row per unique logical mutation; replays add none.
Replays generate zero owner notifications.
Any replay-rejection surface remains branded and non-alarming.
The end-state store diff between original and replayed runs is empty.
Replay fixtures and run-prefixed keys are removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: The collaborative queue survives a full stack restart: entries, order, current position, volume, loop mode, and pause flag all recover and playback resumes.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: With a five-track queue playing track two at volume 80 with loop mode queue, the bot process is killed and restarted; the queue-restored message posts, playback resumes track two, /queue shows the identical five entries and settings, and an empty voice channel would start the auto-leave timer immediately.

assertions.expectedObservation: The queue-restored embed names the restored track and count, audible playback resumes, and /queue output matches the pre-restart snapshot exactly.
The persisted queue object re-reads with identical entries, currentIndex, volume 80, and loopMode queue across the restart.
A recovery audit row links the restored session to the pre-restart session without duplicating track-add history.
A clean recovery within the grace window produces no outage alert.
The restoration message uses the guild brand voice and attribution footer.
Recovery does not re-append entries or re-fire confirmations; queue length is unchanged.
Restart fixtures and run-prefixed state are removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: Concurrent mutations by multiple members keep the queue consistent: no lost entries, no duplicate entries, caps enforced under contention.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Two members fire /play simultaneously while a third removes an entry and a fourth sits at their per-user cap; the final queue contains both new entries exactly once, the removal applied once, the capped member's addition is declined, and currentIndex remains valid.

assertions.expectedObservation: Each successful actor gets exactly one confirmation, the capped member gets the user-cap-reached decline, and /queue reflects a consistent final order.
The persisted queue holds each surviving entry exactly once with a valid currentIndex and correct per-user counts.
One audit row per applied mutation and one for the capacity decline; no phantom rows.
The contention window produces no owner notification.
All concurrent replies remain branded and mutually consistent with the final queue state.
Racing writers never double-append: total entries equal successful logical additions exactly.
Race fixtures and run-prefixed state are removed post-run.

scenarios.promise: Queues and music settings are strictly guild-isolated: activity or configuration in one guild never leaks into another.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Simultaneous sessions in guilds A and B maintain independent queues under separate keys; disabling music in A leaves B playing; B's /queue never shows A's tracks; and A's owner cannot read or write B's music settings.

assertions.expectedObservation: Both guilds play their own queues concurrently and A's disable toggle produces no behavioral change in B.
Queue keys and config rows are keyed by guild id; A's owner context is denied access to B's guild_config row.
Every audit row carries the correct guild id with zero cross-guild rows.
Each guild's notifications route only to its own owner.
Each guild's surfaces render that guild's own brand simultaneously.
Replaying guild A mutations leaves guild B's queue untouched.
Both guilds' run-prefixed resources are independently and completely removed.

scenarios.promise: All run-prefixed collaborative-queue resources are enumerable and fully removed after the suite, leaving only immutable audit rows.
scenarios.expectedOutcome: After the queue suite, a sweep finds zero run-prefixed queue or now-playing keys in Valkey, zero run-prefixed config overrides in guild_config, zero leftover test messages or channels in Discord, and the audit trail intact.

assertions.expectedObservation: Run-created channels and messages are deleted and the bot has left all test voice channels.
Config rows are reverted to pre-run values and no run identifiers remain in stored music settings.
Audit rows from the run remain present and unmodified, honoring never-delete.
Cleanup completes silently with no owner notifications.
Brand configuration is restored to its pre-run state.
Running the sweeper twice is idempotent, reporting zero remaining resources both times.
The final inventory of run-prefixed resources across Discord, Valkey, and Supabase is empty.
